intent.raw_query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September 2026 from London

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, Praia da Marinha, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail for panoramic views, then descend to the secluded cove for a swim among natural rock arches.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour
experiences.description: Visit local Algarve wineries such as Quinta dos Vales or Adega do Cantor near Guia, sampling regional varieties including Negra Mole and Arinto. Guided tours typically include a walk through the vineyards, explanation of the winemaking process, and tasting of 5–6 wines paired with local cheeses and charcuterie.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle by kayak from Praia de Benagil into the famous Algar de Benagil sea cave, one of the most iconic natural wonders in Portugal. A guided kayak tour lets you explore hidden grottos, sea arches, and the cathedral-like interior of the cave with its natural skylight, inaccessible by foot.

experiences.name: Tavira Old Town Cultural Walk & Seafood Lunch
experiences.description: Wander through the charming historic town of Tavira, visiting the Roman bridge, Moorish castle ruins, and over 30 historic churches. End the cultural stroll with a traditional Algarvian seafood lunch at a local tasca, trying cataplana de marisco (seafood stew) and fresh grilled fish paired with local Vinho Verde.

experiences.name: Sagres Sunset Cliffs & Local Wine Tasting
experiences.description: Visit the dramatic Cabo de São Vicente, the southwestern tip of Europe, at golden hour for breathtaking Atlantic sunset views. Afterward, stop at a local wine bar in Sagres village to taste regional Alentejo and Algarve wines, including robust reds and crisp whites, while enjoying the laid-back end-of-the-world atmosphere.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Take the affordable Aerobus or a shared shuttle to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Algarve beachfront area (approx. 30-45 min). Check in, freshen up, and get settled into your room.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night snack at a 24-hour petrol station convenience store or a nearby late-night tasca (local tavern) if open — try a simple bifana (pork sandwich) for under €3.

day_by_day.notes: Keep luggage light for easy transit from the airport. Download the Rede Expressos bus app for cheap local transport options. Exchange some euros before leaving the airport if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up and take your first walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort. Explore the local beach, enjoy the September sea (still warm at ~24°C), and get your bearings around the resort area. Swim and relax on the sand — completely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a local bus to the nearest town center (likely Albufeira or Lagos depending on resort location). Explore the old town, wander through cobblestone streets, visit the local market, and browse budget souvenir shops. Visit a local Adega (wine shop) and pick up a bottle of affordable Algarve regional wine for €4-6.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to the beachfront promenade for sunset views. Enjoy a casual dinner at a local restaurant on the strip.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastel de nata (custard tart, ~€1.20) and a galão (milky coffee, ~€1.50) at a local café near the resort — a classic Portuguese breakfast under €3.
meals.lunch: Find a local tasca in the town center — order prato do dia (dish of the day) which typically includes soup, main, bread, and a drink for €7-9.
meals.dinner: Try a beachfront restaurant offering grilled sardines or a mixed fish plate (petiscos style) for €10-13. Look for restaurants with tourist menus displayed outside.

day_by_day.notes: September is ideal beach weather in the Algarve — warm, sunny, and less crowded than peak summer. Pick up a local SIM card at a tobacco shop (tabacaria) for cheap data.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or rent a cheap bicycle to explore Praia da Marinha or Praia de Benagil — two of the Algarve's most iconic beaches. Swim in the turquoise waters and explore the dramatic limestone cliffs and sea caves along the coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the coastal cliff trail (Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos — Seven Hanging Valleys Trail), a free and stunning 6km hike offering breathtaking views of hidden coves, golden cliffs, and the Atlantic Ocean. The trail is well-marked and manageable for most fitness levels.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Relax on the beach for sunset. Pick up a bottle of local vinho verde or Algarve red wine from a supermarket (Lidl or Pingo Doce) for €4-5 and enjoy it on your balcony or the beach.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the resort or a nearby café — toast with local queijo (cheese) and presunto (cured ham) with coffee for ~€4.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from a local supermarket — fresh bread, local cheese, cured meats, olives, and fruit for under €6 total. Eat on the cliffs or beach.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using supermarket ingredients in the resort kitchen if available, or visit a local churrasqueira (grill house) for a frango assado (roast chicken) meal for €8-10.

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy shoes for the cliff trail and bring sunscreen and water. The Benagil Cave can be seen from kayak tours (€15-20) or via a short swim from the beach if you're a confident swimmer.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning bus to Lagos — one of the Algarve's most charming historic towns. Explore the 15th-century Forte da Ponta da Bandeira (entry ~€3), the old slave market site (Mercado de Escravos, free exterior), and the Igreja de Santo António church.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Praia Dona Ana and Praia do Camilo — two stunning Lagos beaches with dramatic rock formations. Relax, swim, and soak in the scenery. Explore the sea caves and grottos accessible by foot at low tide.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Lagos' lively but affordable nightlife strip on Rua Candido dos Reis. Enjoy a glass of local Algarve wine at a wine bar or a cerveja (beer) at a terrace bar.

meals.breakfast: Café stop in Lagos old town — coffee and tosta mista (toasted ham and cheese sandwich) for ~€3.50.
meals.lunch: Try a local tasca near the market — cataplana de marisco (seafood stew) is a regional specialty; look for lunch menus around €9-11.
meals.dinner: Find a budget-friendly restaurant in Lagos offering bacalhau (salt cod) dishes — bacalhau com broa (cod with cornbread) for ~€11-13.

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is accessible by regional bus (Eva Transportes) for approximately €4-6 one way. Buy a return ticket to save time. The town is very walkable once you arrive.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a relaxed morning at the resort beach. Try stand-up paddleboarding or bodyboarding — many beach rental shops offer boards for €8-12/hour. Practice in the gentle September waves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Algarve winery or wine cooperative for an affordable wine tasting experience. The Algarve has four DOC wine regions — look for Adega do Cantor (associated with Cliff Richard) near Albufeira or local cooperative wineries offering tastings from €5-10 per person.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the beachfront promenade at golden hour. Browse local artisan stalls for handmade ceramics, cork products, and local honey — great affordable souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Try a local padaria (bakery) — fresh bread rolls (papo-secos) with butter and a bica (espresso) for under €2.50.
meals.lunch: Grab a prego no pão (steak sandwich) or a sandes de atum (tuna sandwich) from a snack bar near the beach for €4-6.
meals.dinner: Visit a local adega restaurant near the winery or a seafood restaurant in the resort area — grilled dourada (sea bream) with potatoes and salad for €12-15.

day_by_day.notes: Call ahead to confirm winery visiting hours as smaller operations may require reservations. The Algarve wine region is less famous than Douro or Alentejo but produces excellent, affordable wines.

day_by_day.morning: Take a bus or ferry to Portimão and then continue to Silves — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Visit the impressive red sandstone Castelo de Silves (entry ~€3.30), one of the best-preserved Moorish castles in Portugal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves' charming old town, the Gothic cathedral (Sé de Silves, free entry), and browse the local market. Walk along the Arade River. Visit a local orange grove or cork tree forest on the outskirts — Silves is famous for its citrus fruits.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Algarve coast. Enjoy a quiet evening walk along the beach as the sun sets over the Atlantic.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the resort before departure — or grab something at Portimão bus station café.
meals.lunch: Eat in Silves at a local restaurant — try medronho (arbutus berry spirit) as an aperitif and order a regional lamb or pork dish for €9-12.
meals.dinner: Cook at the resort or visit a local pizzeria/café near the hotel for a light, budget-friendly meal under €10.

day_by_day.notes: Silves is inland — about 15-20km from the coast. The bus journey takes about 45 minutes from Portimão. The town is quieter and more authentically Portuguese than the coastal resorts — a great contrast.

day_by_day.morning: Full beach day! Head to one of the Algarve's famous beaches — Meia Praia (near Lagos, one of the longest beaches in the Algarve at 4km) or Praia de Armação de Pêra. Arrive early for the best spots. Swim, sunbathe, and relax.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the beach area on foot. Look for beach bars (chiringuitos) offering affordable drinks. Try a local água de coco (coconut water) or imperial (draft beer) for €2-3. Build sandcastles, collect shells, or simply read a book.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a beach bonfire if permitted in the area, or join locals for a casual evening on the promenade. Watch the stars from the beach — the Algarve has excellent stargazing conditions away from city lights.

meals.breakfast: Pick up pastries and fruit from a local market or supermarket the night before — eat on the beach.
meals.lunch: Beach bar lunch — prego (steak sandwich) or a tosta with salad and a beer for €7-9.
meals.dinner: Head to a local restaurant near the resort for a classic caldo verde (green soup) starter and grilled fish main — full meal for €12-15.

day_by_day.notes: Midweek beaches in September are noticeably quieter than weekends. September water temperatures in the Algarve average 22-24°C — perfect for swimming.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres — the southwestern tip of Europe at Cape St. Vincent (Cabo de São Vicente). Take a bus from Lagos (or from the nearest town). Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres (entry ~€3) and walk the windswept cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Cabo de São Vicente lighthouse — the most southwestern point of continental Europe. The views are absolutely spectacular. Watch the dramatic waves crashing against 60-meter-high cliffs. Explore the small artisan market near the lighthouse.
day_by_day.evening: Return via Lagos or direct bus. Enjoy a celebratory dinner for reaching the end of Europe.

meals.breakfast: Early café breakfast near the bus station before departure — coffee and croissant for €2-3.
meals.lunch: Eat in Sagres village — fresh tuna (atum) is a local specialty; try a tuna steak with potatoes for €10-13 at a local restaurant.
meals.dinner: Back at the resort area — treat yourself to a slightly nicer seafood dinner at a local restaurant, keeping it under €18 with a glass of local wine.

day_by_day.notes: Sagres can be windy even in September — bring a light jacket. The bus journey from Lagos to Sagres takes about 1 hour and costs approximately €4-5. Check Eva Transportes schedules in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the local Algarve food market (mercado) in the nearest town. Browse stalls selling fresh fish, local cheeses, honey, figs, almonds, carob, and seasonal produce. Pick up local snacks and ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local quinta (farm estate) for an informal wine or medronho tasting. Many Algarve quintas offer informal tours and tastings for free or minimal cost (€5-8). Alternatively, visit a local cooperative winery in Lagoa — the Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa is one of the oldest in the Algarve.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a local fado night if available at a nearby restaurant or cultural center — some venues offer free or low-cost fado performances with dinner. Ask the hotel reception for recommendations.

meals.breakfast: Buy fresh produce at the morning market — local figs, almonds, cheese, and bread for a picnic-style breakfast under €5.
meals.lunch: Market lunch — try a fresh grilled fish from a market stall or a nearby tasca for €8-10.
meals.dinner: Fado dinner or a local restaurant specializing in petiscos (Portuguese tapas) — share several small dishes for €12-16 per person.

day_by_day.notes: September is harvest season in the Algarve — you may find local grape harvest festivals (vindimas) happening in nearby villages, which are free and culturally rich experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning kayaking or stand-up paddleboard tour along the Algarve coastline to explore sea caves and grottos up close. Many operators offer guided kayak tours from €20-25 per person, including the famous Benagil Cave tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the kayak tour, relax on a quieter beach. Explore tide pools and rock formations along the coast. Collect sea glass or shells as free souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a beachfront bar — happy hour deals often available from 5-7pm. Try a local licor de amêndoa amarga (bitter almond liqueur) or a simple gin and tonic with local herbs.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the kayak tour — banana, energy bar, and coffee from a café for ~€3.
meals.lunch: Post-kayak meal at a beachside snack bar — toasted sandwich and fresh juice for €5-7.
meals.dinner: Visit a local churrasqueira for grilled chicken, piri-piri style — a full meal with sides for €9-11.

day_by_day.notes: Book kayak tours at least one day in advance, especially for Benagil Cave tours which are popular even in September. Wear reef shoes for rocky coastline exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Loulé — an authentic inland Algarve town known for its Moorish architecture and vibrant Saturday market (if visiting on a Saturday) or the permanent covered market. Explore the Castelo de Loulé and the old medina-style streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Browse Loulé's famous market for local crafts, copperware, leather goods, and regional food products. Visit the Nossa Senhora da Conceição church built on a former mosque. Walk the town's charming streets and enjoy the slower pace of inland Algarve life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a final evening swim and sunset on the beach. Buy a bottle of local wine from a supermarket and enjoy it on the beach or balcony.

meals.breakfast: Eat at a café near the resort before the bus journey to Loulé.
meals.lunch: Loulé market lunch — try local specialties like carob-based products, almond sweets (Dom Rodrigos), and a simple market lunch for €7-10.
meals.dinner: Back at the resort area — simple supermarket meal or a local café dinner for under €10.

day_by_day.notes: Loulé is about 15km inland from the coast. Buses run regularly from Albufeira and Faro. The Saturday market is the largest and most vibrant but the permanent covered market is open daily.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach morning — return to your favorite beach discovered during the trip. Take a long swim, walk the shoreline one last time, and soak in the Algarve sunshine. Collect any final shells or sea glass as memories.
day_by_day.afternoon: Do any remaining souvenir shopping — look for affordable Portuguese gifts: cork products (wallets, bags), azulejo (tile) magnets, local honey, almond sweets, ginjinha (cherry liqueur), and regional wines. Pingo Doce or Lidl supermarkets offer great value on food souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the best local restaurant you discovered during the trip. Splurge slightly on a special cataplana dish or a mixed seafood platter to celebrate the end of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Final resort or café breakfast — enjoy a leisurely coffee and pastel de nata one last time.
meals.lunch: Beach bar lunch — keep it light and casual, enjoying the last hours of sunshine.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner — cataplana de marisco (seafood stew) for two or a mixed grilled fish platter, with a bottle of local Algarve wine. Budget €18-22 for a special send-off meal.

day_by_day.notes: Pack souvenirs carefully — Portuguese wine, olive oil, and liqueurs are popular but check airline liquid restrictions. Consider shipping heavier items home via CTT (Portuguese postal service) if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a last breakfast at the resort. Take a short final walk on the beach. Pack and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Store luggage at the hotel reception if your departure is later in the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, take a final stroll through the local area or relax at the resort pool/beach. Head to Faro Airport via Aerobus or shared shuttle (book the day before at the hotel reception for best rates — approximately €15-20 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days exploring the beaches, wines, and culture of the beautiful Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Final Portuguese breakfast at the resort or a nearby café — coffee, pastel de nata, and fresh orange juice (the Algarve is famous for its oranges) for ~€4.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the hotel or at Faro Airport — keep it simple and budget-friendly.
meals.dinner: Airport meal or inflight — pick up a sandwich and snacks from a supermarket before heading to the airport to save money.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5 hours before your flight for check-in and security at Faro Airport. The Aerobus runs regularly from major Algarve towns to the airport. Keep €10-15 in cash for any last-minute expenses or tips. Total estimated daily budget excluding accommodation: €30-50/day covering meals, transport, and activities.

trip_options.title: Classic Portugal Algarve Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, Praia da Marinha, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail for panoramic views, then descend to the secluded cove for a swim among natural rock arches.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort (approx. 40-60 min drive depending on exact location). Check in, freshen up, and unwind with a welcome drink at the hotel bar if still open.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a light snack at the airport or hotel bar upon arrival — look for petiscos (Portuguese tapas) if available

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Pre-arrange airport transfer with your hotel to avoid taxi stress late at night. Pack a snack in your carry-on for after landing. Rest well — big adventures start tomorrow!

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Spend the morning getting oriented — take a slow walk along the beachfront promenade near the hotel, dip your toes in the Atlantic, and soak in the Algarve atmosphere for the first time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest local beach (likely Meia Praia or a beach adjacent to your resort area). Rent a sun lounger, swim in the warm September sea, and explore the shoreline on foot. September is ideal — crowds have thinned but the water is still warm (~22°C).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the nearest town centre (Lagos or Portimão depending on resort location) for your first proper Portuguese dinner. Explore the old town streets and enjoy the warm evening air.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy fresh pastéis de nata, local cheeses, and fruit
meals.lunch: Casual beach snack bar (chiringuito) near the resort — try a grilled sardine sandwich (prego de sardinha) and a cold Super Bock beer (~€8-12)
meals.dinner: A Forja (Lagos) or similar mid-range local tasca — order grilled sea bass (robalo grelhado) or cataplana de marisco (seafood stew) (~€18-25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Buy a local SIM card or activate an eSIM today for navigation and restaurant bookings. Pick up sunscreen and any beach essentials at a local pharmacy (farmácia).

day_by_day.morning: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim — one of the Algarve's crown jewels. Start early (9:00 AM) to beat any remaining summer visitors. The dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea arches, and crystal-clear turquoise coves are breathtaking. Hike the clifftop trail (approx. 2km loop) and descend to the beach for a swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Seven Hanging Valleys Trail (Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos) — a stunning 5.7km clifftop walk between Praia de Vale Centeanes and Praia da Marinha. Stop at viewpoints (miradouros) for photos. Alternatively, rent a kayak or join a boat tour from Benagil to see the famous Benagil Sea Cave from the water.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to shower and relax. Head to Carvoeiro village for a sunset cocktail at a clifftop bar, then dinner in the charming village square.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab a pastel de nata and coffee at a local café before the hike (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks or a light meal at the beach snack bar near Praia da Marinha — grilled chicken wrap or fresh fruit (~€8-10)
meals.dinner: O Castelo restaurant in Carvoeiro or similar — try açorda de marisco (seafood bread stew) or grilled dorado (dourada) with local white wine (~€20-28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy shoes for the coastal hike — the limestone paths can be uneven. Bring plenty of water, sunscreen, and a hat. Book the Benagil boat tour in advance as September slots still fill up. Praia da Marinha has limited parking — arrive early or take a taxi/rideshare.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or take a local bus to Lagos (approx. 20-30 min west). Explore the historic old town — walk the ancient city walls, visit Igreja de Santo António (a stunning baroque church), and browse the covered market (Mercado de Lagos) for local produce, cheeses, and cured meats.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Lagos's famous grottos and beaches — Praia Dona Ana, Praia do Camilo, and the sea caves at Ponta da Piedade. Hire a kayak or paddleboard to explore the golden rock formations and hidden sea caves at water level. This is one of the most photogenic spots in the Algarve.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Lagos for dinner and evening entertainment. The town has a vibrant but relaxed nightlife scene perfect for a mid-range traveller.

meals.breakfast: Café Combatentes or similar café in Lagos old town — galão (milky coffee) and a tosta mista (toasted ham and cheese) (~€4-6)
meals.lunch: : O Camilo restaurant near Praia do Camilo — fresh grilled fish with a view over the cliffs (~€15-22 per person)
meals.dinner: Casinha do Petisco (Lagos) — excellent mid-range Portuguese cuisine, try the bacalhau com broa (salt cod with cornbread crust) and a glass of Alentejo red wine (~€18-25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The market in Lagos is best visited in the morning when it's fully stocked. Ponta da Piedade kayak tours are weather-dependent — check conditions the morning of. Wear water shoes for the sea cave exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting day begins! Drive inland to the Algarve wine region around Lagoa or Silves (approx. 20-30 min). Visit Adega do Cantor (founded by Cliff Richard) or Quinta dos Vales — two of the most acclaimed Algarve wineries. Take a guided cellar tour and taste local varietals including Negra Mole and Crato Branco.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to a second winery — try Quinta da Penina or Morgado do Quintão near Lagoa. These family-run estates offer intimate tastings with panoramic vineyard views. Purchase a few bottles to enjoy during the trip. Afterwards, explore the medieval town of Silves — the old Moorish capital of the Algarve — and walk up to the impressive red sandstone castle (Castelo de Silves).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort or nearby town for a relaxed dinner. Pair your meal with one of the wines you purchased today.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fuel up before the wine tasting day
meals.lunch: Wine and cheese pairing lunch at one of the wineries — most offer a petiscos platter with local cheeses, charcuterie, and bread (~€15-20 per person including wine)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui (Silves) — a legendary seafood restaurant, try the cataplana de amêijoas (clam stew) or fresh grilled tiger prawns (~€22-30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book winery tours in advance — weekend slots fill up quickly. Designate a driver or arrange a taxi/wine tour service so everyone can enjoy the tastings freely. Quinta dos Vales offers particularly scenic vineyard views perfect for photos.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed beach morning at the resort or a nearby quiet cove. September Sundays are peaceful — find a secluded spot, read, swim, and recharge. Try snorkelling if the resort offers equipment rental — the Algarve's rocky coves are teeming with marine life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Portimão (approx. 15-25 min) and visit Praia da Rocha — a wide, dramatic beach backed by towering ochre cliffs. Walk the clifftop promenade, browse the Sunday market stalls, and visit the Museu de Portimão (free on Sundays) — a fascinating museum built inside a converted fish cannery.
day_by_day.evening: Portimão is famous for its grilled sardines (sardinhas assadas) — enjoy them fresh off the grill at a riverside restaurant along the Rio Arade. This is a quintessential Algarve Sunday evening experience.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed hotel breakfast or fresh fruit and yogurt from a local supermarket enjoyed on your balcony
meals.lunch: Light beach snack — bifanas (pork rolls) or a fresh salad from a beach kiosk (~€6-9)
meals.dinner: Taberna da Maré (Portimão) or a riverside tasca — grilled sardines, piri piri chicken, and a cold Sagres beer (~€15-20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Museu de Portimão is free on Sunday afternoons — highly recommended, especially interesting for the canning industry history. The riverside area in Portimão has a great Sunday evening atmosphere with live music sometimes playing in summer/early autumn.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip east to Faro — the Algarve's capital and a vastly underrated city. Explore the beautiful Cidade Velha (Old Town) surrounded by Roman walls, visit the Sé Cathedral and climb the bell tower for panoramic views, and browse the Museu Municipal de Faro.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a ferry from Faro marina to the Ria Formosa Natural Park — a stunning lagoon system of barrier islands, salt marshes, and tidal flats. Spend the afternoon on Ilha Deserta (Desert Island) or Ilha de Faro — pristine, uncrowded beaches backed by dunes. The water in the lagoon is calm and warm, ideal for swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Faro for dinner in the old town before driving back to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria Gardy (Faro) — a historic café in the old town, try the local queijinhos (small cheese pastries) and a bica (espresso) (~€4-5)
meals.lunch: Picnic on Ilha Deserta — buy fresh bread, local cheese, presunto (cured ham), and fruit from the Faro market before taking the ferry (~€10-12 self-catered)
meals.dinner: Faz Gostos restaurant (Faro old town) — elegant but affordable, try the arroz de lingueirão (razor clam rice) or pork with clams (carne de porco à alentejana) (~€20-28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ferry to Ilha Deserta runs regularly from Faro marina — check the last return time to avoid being stranded. Faro is about 40-60 min drive east of most Algarve resorts. Parking near the old town is available at the marina car park.

day_by_day.morning: Second wine tasting excursion — this time head to the Alentejo wine region just north of the Algarve (approx. 1.5-2 hours drive). Visit Herdade do Esporão or Herdade dos Grous near Beja — world-class wineries with stunning estates, organic vineyards, and exceptional tastings of Alentejo's bold reds and fresh whites.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the whitewashed villages of the lower Alentejo — stop at Mértola, a stunning hilltop village with a castle and one of Portugal's only Moorish-style churches. Walk the ancient walls and enjoy the dramatic views over the Guadiana River.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to the resort (allow 1.5-2 hours). Enjoy a quiet dinner at the hotel or a nearby restaurant — let the day's wine and scenery sink in.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before the drive north
meals.lunch: Estate lunch at the winery — Herdade do Esporão has an excellent restaurant with farm-to-table cuisine and wine pairings (~€25-35 per person, book in advance)
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant or a local tasca near the resort — keep it simple after a long day, try a grilled pork secreto (Iberian pork) with local potatoes (~€16-22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is a longer driving day — consider hiring a driver or joining an organised wine tour from Portimão or Lagos. Herdade do Esporão's restaurant requires advance booking. Bring a cooler bag to transport purchased wine bottles safely.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the western Algarve — drive to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente (approx. 45-60 min west). Cabo de São Vicente is the southwesternmost point of mainland Europe — a dramatic, windswept headland with a lighthouse and breathtaking Atlantic views. Visit the Fortaleza de Sagres, a historic fortress with a mysterious wind compass (rosa dos ventos) carved into the ground.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia do Beliche or Praia da Mareta near Sagres — wilder, more rugged beaches with powerful Atlantic swells. These are popular with surfers but also offer calm swimming areas. The water here is slightly cooler than the south coast but incredibly clear. Alternatively, take a surf lesson at one of the local surf schools.
day_by_day.evening: Have dinner in Sagres village — a small, authentic fishing village with excellent seafood restaurants and a laid-back surfer vibe.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab a coffee and pastry at a café in Vila do Bispo on the drive to Sagres
meals.lunch: Nortada restaurant (Sagres) or a beach café — fresh tuna steak (bife de atum) is a Sagres speciality (~€14-18 per person)
meals.dinner: A Tasca (Sagres) — a beloved local restaurant, try the caldeirada de peixe (traditional fish stew) with crusty bread and a glass of vinho verde (~€18-24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Cabo de São Vicente can be very windy — bring a light jacket even in September. The drive along the western Algarve coast (N268) is one of Portugal's most scenic routes. Sagres has a very different, wilder atmosphere compared to the eastern Algarve — embrace it!

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at the resort — enjoy a final long swim, paddleboard session, or yoga on the beach. Take time to sit and appreciate the Algarve's stunning scenery that you've been rushing past all week.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local spa or wellness centre near the resort for a traditional massage or treatment — many mid-range resorts offer day spa access. Alternatively, explore a local weekly market (mercado) if one is running nearby — perfect for picking up artisan ceramics, local honey, almonds, and carob products as souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Take a sunset boat cruise from the nearest marina (Portimão, Lagos, or Vilamoura) — many operators offer 2-hour sunset catamaran trips with wine and snacks included. One of the most magical Algarve experiences.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast — treat yourself to the full spread
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort — fresh salad, grilled vegetables, and a glass of local rosé (~€12-16)
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly tonight — Restaurante Sueste (Ferragudo) or a waterfront restaurant with views — try the arroz de tamboril (monkfish rice) or lobster cataplana (~€28-38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the sunset boat cruise at least 2-3 days in advance. Many tours depart from Portimão or Lagos and last 2 hours — prices are typically €35-50 per person including drinks. This is a highlight not to be missed!

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Vilamoura (east of the resort, approx. 30-45 min) — the Algarve's most glamorous resort town. Walk the stunning marina, watch the luxury yachts, and visit the Roman ruins of Cerro da Vila (a well-preserved 1st-century Roman villa and museum right in the town centre).
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Praia de Vilamoura or Praia da Falésia — the latter is one of the Algarve's most dramatic beaches, stretching 6km with towering red and ochre cliffs. Walk the full length if energy allows. The beach is quieter in late September and absolutely stunning.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Vilamoura's marina atmosphere for dinner — plenty of excellent mid-range options along the waterfront. This is a great people-watching spot on a Friday evening.

meals.breakfast: Café Concerto or a marina café in Vilamoura — fresh orange juice, croissants, and a galão (~€5-7)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Praia da Falésia — grilled chicken piri piri wrap and a cold drink (~€10-13)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Akvavit (Vilamoura marina) or similar — try the grilled tiger prawns with garlic and lemon or the fresh fish of the day (~€22-30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Praia da Falésia is accessed via a wooden boardwalk down the cliffs — bring good footwear. The beach has no facilities at the far end so bring water and snacks. The Roman ruins at Cerro da Vila are surprisingly impressive and rarely crowded — a hidden gem.

day_by_day.morning: Final wine experience — visit a local wine shop or adega in the nearest town and join a structured wine and cheese tasting session (many wine shops offer these). Stock up on bottles of Algarve and Alentejo wine to bring home. Also visit a local deli for regional products — medronho (arbutus berry brandy), local almonds, carob chocolate, and flor de sal sea salt make excellent gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to your favourite beach of the trip for one last long swim and afternoon on the sand. Reflect on the journey, take final photos, and enjoy the warm September Algarve sun. Try a water sport you haven't done yet — jet ski, parasailing, or a banana boat ride for some fun.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — choose your favourite restaurant from the trip or try somewhere special you've been saving. Celebrate the end of a wonderful 13-day journey through the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — enjoy it fully knowing it's one of the last
meals.lunch: Beach picnic with goods purchased from the morning market and deli — local cheese, presunto, olives, bread, and a bottle of local wine on the sand (~€15 self-catered)
meals.dinner: Splurge farewell dinner — Vila Joya (Albufeira, 2 Michelin stars) for a special occasion, or a beloved local restaurant revisited — toast with a bottle of Alentejo red and medronho digestif (~€35-50 per person for a special meal)

day_by_day.notes: Check airline regulations for bringing wine home — typically 2 bottles in checked luggage wrapped securely. Many wine shops offer vacuum-sealed packaging. Buy medronho from a local producer rather than a tourist shop for better quality and price.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a slow last breakfast at the resort. Pack, check out, and take one final walk on the beach or along the promenade. Breathe in the salt air and commit the view to memory.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your flight time, either explore Faro city one more time (if departing in the evening) or head directly to Faro Airport. Allow extra time for car return if hired, and arrive at the airport at least 2 hours before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Carry the warmth of the Algarve — its golden cliffs, turquoise sea, world-class wines, and generous cuisine — home with you.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — savour every pastéis de nata
meals.lunch: Café/restaurant near Faro Airport or in Faro city centre if time allows — a final bifana (pork roll) or tosta mista with coffee (~€5-8)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00-12:00 — confirm with the hotel. Faro Airport is small but can get busy on Sunday afternoons in September. Security queues can be longer than expected — allow ample time. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, Praia da Marinha, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail for panoramic views, then descend to the secluded cove for a swim among natural rock arches.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour
experiences.description: Visit local Algarve wineries such as Quinta dos Vales or Adega do Cantor near Guia, sampling regional varieties including Negra Mole and Arinto. Guided tours typically include a walk through the vineyards, explanation of the winemaking process, and tasting of 5–6 wines paired with local cheeses and charcuterie.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle by kayak from Praia de Benagil into the famous Algar de Benagil sea cave, one of the most iconic natural wonders in Portugal. A guided kayak tour lets you explore hidden grottos, sea arches, and the cathedral-like interior of the cave with its natural skylight, inaccessible by foot.

experiences.name: Tavira Old Town Cultural Walk & Seafood Lunch
experiences.description: Wander through the charming historic town of Tavira, visiting the Roman bridge, Moorish castle ruins, and over 30 historic churches. End the cultural stroll with a traditional Algarvian seafood lunch at a local tasca, trying cataplana de marisco (seafood stew) and fresh grilled fish paired with local Vinho Verde.

experiences.name: Sagres Sunset Cliffs & Local Wine Tasting
experiences.description: Visit the dramatic Cabo de São Vicente, the southwestern tip of Europe, at golden hour for breathtaking Atlantic sunset views. Afterward, stop at a local wine bar in Sagres village to taste regional Alentejo and Algarve wines, including robust reds and crisp whites, while enjoying the laid-back end-of-the-world atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged by Aegean Bliss Resort picks you up curbside. Check in to your Beachfront suite, enjoy a welcome amenity of chilled Alentejo wine and local cheese board prepared by the resort. Settle in and unwind on your private terrace listening to the Atlantic.

meals.breakfast: N/A – In flight
meals.lunch: N/A – In flight
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome cheese and charcuterie board with regional wines in-suite, courtesy of Aegean Bliss Resort

day_by_day.notes: Confirm private airport transfer with resort concierge at least 48 hours before arrival. Pack light carry-on essentials for easy late-night check-in. No activities scheduled given the late arrival time.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely gourmet breakfast at the resort's beachfront restaurant. Spend the late morning exploring the resort's private beach, acclimating to the Algarve's warm September sun and turquoise waters. Arrange a complimentary beach cabana with the concierge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the resort's shuttle or a private car to Praia da Marinha for the Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim experience. Explore the dramatic golden limestone cliffs, hidden sea arches, and crystal-clear coves. Swim in the sheltered turquoise waters and photograph the iconic rock formations. A private guide can be arranged through the concierge for a more curated experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a sunset cocktail at the rooftop bar overlooking the Atlantic. Dine at a premium local restaurant such as Ocean Restaurant at Vila Vita Parc (2 Michelin stars) in Porches for an extraordinary seafood tasting menu showcasing Algarve's finest ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort's beachfront restaurant – fresh pastries, smoked salmon, local cheeses, tropical fruits, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch box prepared by the resort to enjoy at Praia da Marinha – grilled chicken wraps, local olives, fruit, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Ocean Restaurant at Vila Vita Parc, Porches – Michelin-starred seafood tasting menu with paired Portuguese wines (reserve in advance)

day_by_day.notes: Praia da Marinha is approximately 10–15 minutes by car from most Algarve beachfront resorts. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the coastal trail. The path can be uneven; a private guide enhances safety and storytelling.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the day with an early breakfast at the resort followed by the Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour. Depart from Praia de Benagil, paddling into the legendary Algar de Benagil sea cave – one of the world's most photographed natural wonders. A private guided kayak session ensures an exclusive, crowd-free experience at the cave. September light through the cave's oculus is spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the kayak tour, relax on Praia de Benagil beach for a light lunch at a nearby café. In the mid-afternoon, return to the resort for a spa treatment at Aegean Bliss Resort's wellness center – opt for a signature Portuguese-inspired massage using local argan and almond oils to soothe kayaking muscles.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset aperitivo on your private beachfront terrace. Dinner at Henrique Leis (Michelin-starred, Almancil) – a sophisticated menu blending French technique with Portuguese ingredients in an intimate villa setting.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the resort – eggs benedict, fresh açorda bread, artisanal jams, and Algarve orange juice
meals.lunch: Light seafood lunch at a beachside café near Praia de Benagil – grilled sardines, salad, and local Sagres beer or sparkling water
meals.dinner: Henrique Leis, Almancil – Michelin-starred contemporary cuisine with an exceptional Portuguese wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book the private kayak tour at least 3–4 days in advance, especially in September. The cave is best visited in the morning when light streams through the oculus. The resort spa should be booked the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a relaxed breakfast on your terrace. Morning at leisure at the resort – take a sunrise swim, practice yoga on the beach (request the resort's yoga instructor), or simply read by the pool. This is a gentle recovery day after the kayak adventure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Embark on the Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour. A private chauffeured car takes you to Quinta dos Vales near Estômbar, a boutique winery set among rolling hills. Tour the vineyards, learn about the unique Algarve terroir, and enjoy a guided tasting of their award-winning reds, whites, and rosés paired with local charcuterie. Optionally extend the visit to Adega do Cantor near Guia for a second tasting experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort in time for a golden-hour swim. Dine at Restaurante Sueste in Ferragudo – a premium waterfront restaurant renowned for its fresh catch, grilled fish, and sophisticated wine list overlooking the Arade River estuary.

meals.breakfast: Terrace breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort – fresh fruit platter, yogurt with local honey, croissants, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Wine and charcuterie pairing at Quinta dos Vales – artisanal cheeses, cured meats, olives, and freshly baked bread served in the winery's estate gardens
meals.dinner: Restaurante Sueste, Ferragudo – fresh Atlantic fish, tiger prawns, and Algarve cataplana stew with premium Alentejo wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Confirm wine tour booking with Quinta dos Vales directly or through the resort concierge. September is harvest season, making this an especially immersive winery visit. Designated driver or private chauffeur is essential for the wine tour.

day_by_day.morning: Early gourmet breakfast at the resort. Drive west to Sagres for the Sagres Sunset Cliffs & Local Wine Tasting experience – visit the legendary Cabo de São Vicente, the southwestern tip of continental Europe. Walk the windswept clifftops, explore the historic Fortaleza de Sagres, and absorb the raw, dramatic beauty of this UNESCO-recognized landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy lunch in the charming village of Sagres at a premium local restaurant. Spend the afternoon exploring the coastline around Sagres, including Praia do Beliche and Praia da Baleeira – secluded beaches with wild Atlantic character. A private boat charter from Sagres for a coastal tour of the cliffs is an excellent optional upgrade.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Cabo de São Vicente for the golden-hour sunset – arguably one of Europe's most spectacular. Participate in the included local wine tasting at a nearby quinta or wine bar, sampling regional Algarve and Alentejo wines as the sun dips below the Atlantic horizon. Return to the resort for a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast – smoked salmon bagels, avocado toast, fresh juices, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: A Sagres – premium seafood restaurant in Sagres village, featuring freshly caught grilled fish, percebes (barnacles), and local wines
meals.dinner: In-resort dining at Aegean Bliss Resort's signature restaurant – request the chef's tasting menu for a curated Algarve experience

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is approximately 1.5–2 hours from the central Algarve by car. Depart early to maximize time. The sunset at Cabo de São Vicente is world-famous – arrive 30–45 minutes before sunset for best positioning. Book a private boat charter in advance if desired.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely Sunday breakfast at the resort. Spend the morning at the resort's private beach – rent a paddleboard or snorkel set from the watersports desk. The September sea is warm and calm, ideal for relaxed water activities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private yacht charter afternoon – arrange through the resort concierge a half-day luxury sailing or motor yacht excursion along the Algarve's golden coastline. Visit hidden sea caves, anchor in secluded coves, and enjoy a chilled bottle of vinho verde on deck. This is a quintessential premium Algarve experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails at the resort's rooftop bar. Dinner at Gusto by Heinz Beck at Conrad Algarve (Michelin-starred, Almancil) – innovative Mediterranean-Portuguese cuisine from the acclaimed German chef in an elegant, art-filled dining room.

meals.breakfast: Champagne Sunday brunch at the resort – oysters, smoked fish, carved meats, pastries, and unlimited Algarve sparkling wine
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch on the yacht – chilled seafood platter, artisanal sandwiches, fresh fruit, and chilled white wine served by the yacht crew
meals.dinner: Gusto by Heinz Beck, Conrad Algarve, Almancil – Michelin-starred contemporary cuisine with world-class wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book the private yacht charter at least one week in advance through the resort concierge or a local charter company such as Dream Wave Algarve or Algarve Luxury Charters. Half-day charters typically run 4–5 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast followed by a morning wine-focused excursion to the Alentejo wine region – a scenic 1.5-hour drive north from the Algarve. Visit Herdade do Esporão or Herdade dos Grous near Beja, two of Portugal's most prestigious wine estates. Enjoy a cellar tour, barrel tasting, and a deep dive into Alentejo's bold red wines and elegant whites.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a farm-to-table lunch on the estate grounds, surrounded by cork oak trees and vineyards. After lunch, visit a second estate or explore the medieval town of Beja briefly before heading back south to the Algarve.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxed evening. Enjoy a private in-suite dinner arranged by the resort – a curated menu prepared by the executive chef featuring the Alentejo wines you tasted earlier, paired with local Algarve ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Light resort breakfast – yogurt parfait, fresh fruit, pastries, and espresso
meals.lunch: Estate lunch at Herdade do Esporão or Herdade dos Grous – seasonal farm-to-table menu with estate wine pairings in a stunning rural setting
meals.dinner: Private in-suite chef's dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort – a romantic, personalized 5-course tasting menu with Alentejo wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: The Alentejo day trip requires an early start. Arrange a private driver for the round trip. Book estate visits in advance as premium experiences fill up quickly, especially during September harvest season.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at the resort. After breakfast, visit the resort's spa for a full morning of wellness – begin with a hammam ritual, followed by a couples' or solo deep-tissue massage, and finish with a hydrotherapy circuit. A perfect mid-trip recharge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive east to Tavira for the Tavira Old Town Cultural Walk & Seafood Lunch experience. Wander through one of the Algarve's most charming and authentic towns – cross the Roman bridge, explore the Moorish castle ruins, visit the Igreja de Santa Maria do Castelo, and browse the vibrant local market. A private guide brings history to life.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a premium seafood lunch in Tavira (served as a late afternoon meal) before returning to the resort for sunset cocktails. Dine casually at the resort's beach bar – grilled octopus, fresh prawns, and a bottle of crisp Alvarinho white wine under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the resort – eggs any style, fresh pastries, local honey, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Quatro Águas, Tavira – one of the Algarve's finest seafood restaurants, overlooking the Ria Formosa lagoon, serving fresh oysters, clams, and grilled fish
meals.dinner: Casual beachfront dining at Aegean Bliss Resort's beach bar – grilled octopus, tiger prawns, Algarve cheese board, and chilled Alvarinho

day_by_day.notes: Tavira is approximately 45–60 minutes east of the central Algarve. A private driver allows you to enjoy wine at lunch without concern. Tavira is one of the most authentically preserved Moorish towns in Portugal – highly recommended for history lovers.

day_by_day.morning: Morning beach session at the resort's private beach. Rent a kayak or stand-up paddleboard for a self-guided coastal exploration along the shoreline. The September sea conditions are typically calm and warm – ideal for independent water adventures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Silves, the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Explore the impressive red sandstone Silves Castle, the Gothic cathedral, and the charming riverside town. Silves is also surrounded by citrus and almond groves and small quintas producing local wines – stop at a local adega for an informal tasting.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for sunset. Dinner at Restaurante Alameda in Silves (if timing allows) or at a premium Portimão waterfront restaurant – Restaurante Titanic in Portimão is a local institution for grilled fish and fresh seafood in an upscale setting.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – smoked salmon, poached eggs, fresh açorda bread, and seasonal fruit bowl
meals.lunch: Marisqueira Rui, Silves – a legendary local seafood restaurant known for its cataplana and freshly grilled fish, favored by discerning locals and visitors alike
meals.dinner: Restaurante Titanic, Portimão – premium grilled fish, shellfish, and Algarve specialties with a well-curated Portuguese wine list

day_by_day.notes: Silves is approximately 20–30 minutes inland from the coast. The castle is best visited in the afternoon when morning tour groups have departed. Combine with a short walk along the Arade River for a picturesque experience.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the day with a sunrise beach walk before breakfast. After a full resort breakfast, depart for a private guided snorkeling tour of the Algarve's marine reserves. The waters around Praia da Marinha and Ponta da Piedade host rich marine life including octopus, sea bream, and colorful reef fish. A private boat with snorkel gear and a marine biologist guide is the premium way to experience this.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the dramatic Ponta da Piedade rock formations near Lagos by private boat – golden limestone towers, sea arches, and hidden grottos at their most photogenic in afternoon light. Explore Lagos old town briefly: the historic slave market building (Mercado de Escravos), the Igreja de Santo António, and the charming cobblestone streets.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a Lagos rooftop bar. Dinner at Casinha do Petisco, Lagos – an intimate, chef-driven restaurant with creative takes on traditional Algarve cuisine using the freshest local ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet resort breakfast – fresh pastries, eggs benedict with smoked salmon, tropical fruit, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on the boat during the snorkeling and Ponta da Piedade tour – gourmet sandwiches, fresh fruit, sparkling water, and chilled rosé prepared by the resort
meals.dinner: Casinha do Petisco, Lagos – creative Algarve cuisine in an intimate setting, with an excellent selection of regional wines

day_by_day.notes: Book the private snorkeling and boat tour through the resort concierge or a reputable Lagos-based operator. September visibility is excellent for snorkeling. Lagos is approximately 30–40 minutes from the central Algarve.

day_by_day.morning: Full spa morning at Aegean Bliss Resort – indulge in a premium facial, body wrap using local carob and almond extracts, and a relaxing float session. This is a dedicated wellness day to recharge before the final stretch of the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private cooking class at a local Algarve quinta or culinary studio. Learn to prepare traditional Algarve dishes: cataplana de marisco (shellfish stew), amêijoas à Bulhão Pato (clams), and Dom Rodrigo almond sweets. The class includes a guided wine pairing with regional wines and ends with a shared meal of everything you've prepared.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxed evening. Enjoy a private sunset champagne experience on the beach arranged by the concierge – a table set on the sand with Champagne or Portuguese espumante, strawberries, and artisanal chocolates. Dinner at the resort's signature restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Light spa-day breakfast at the resort – green smoothie, granola with local honey, fresh fruit, and herbal tea
meals.lunch: Cooking class meal – enjoy the dishes you prepared during the afternoon class, paired with Algarve wines
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort signature restaurant – chef's tasting menu with wine pairing, celebrating your penultimate full day in the Algarve

day_by_day.notes: Book the private cooking class through the resort concierge or directly with a local culinary school such as Algarve Cooking Class or a quinta that offers the experience. Classes typically run 3–4 hours.

day_by_day.morning: One final morning of the Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour – this time focused on a different producer. Visit Adega do Cantor (founded by Sir Cliff Richard) near Guia, a premium boutique winery producing elegant reds and whites. Enjoy a private barrel room tour and seated tasting with the winemaker. Purchase bottles to take home as souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a final afternoon at the private beach. Swim, paddleboard, or simply relax in a luxury cabana with chilled wine and fresh fruit. Visit the resort's boutique for any last-minute Algarve artisan gifts – local ceramics, almond products, and premium olive oils.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner at the resort or at a top Algarve restaurant. Recommend booking a private dining experience on the beach at Aegean Bliss Resort – a candlelit table set on the sand with a personalized 7-course tasting menu crafted by the executive chef, paired with the finest Portuguese wines from the cellar.

meals.breakfast: Celebratory resort breakfast – freshly baked pastries, smoked fish, premium cheeses, fresh juices, and Cava or local espumante
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort's beach bar after the winery visit – grilled vegetables, hummus, artisan bread, and a glass of the Adega do Cantor wine you just tasted
meals.dinner: Private beach candlelit farewell dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort – 7-course chef's tasting menu with premium Portuguese wine pairing, personalized to your preferences

day_by_day.notes: Confirm the private beach dinner with the resort concierge at least 3 days in advance. This is a signature luxury experience and one of the most memorable ways to end the trip. Adega do Cantor requires advance booking for private tours.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the beach. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the resort – take your time, savor every bite, and reflect on 13 extraordinary days in the Algarve. Pack and prepare for checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, enjoy a final swim or pool session. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. The resort concierge arranges a private luxury transfer to Faro Airport. Browse Faro Airport's duty-free for last-minute Portuguese wine, ginjinha, or Pastéis de Belém to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Carry the memories of golden cliffs, sea caves, world-class wines, and Atlantic sunsets.

meals.breakfast: Final gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort – the full spread, enjoyed slowly and savored
meals.lunch: Light airport lunch at Faro Airport or a quick stop at a café in Faro old town if time allows – pastel de nata, espresso, and a light sandwich
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time and private transfer to Faro Airport with the concierge the evening before. Allow at least 2 hours before your flight for airport procedures. Consider purchasing a selection of Algarve wines and local artisan products at the airport or resort boutique as gifts.
